work.title: Review variance()/stdev() implementation in calc
work.result: APPROVE: variance() is population variance (divide by n, not n-1). For [1, 2, 3, 4] the squared deviations sum to 5 and 5/4 is 1.25. stdev() returns variance(xs) ** 0.5. Both call list(xs) before any second pass, so a generator is consumed once, and both raise ValueError on empty input. Style matches mean(): no type hints, no docstrings, same list / empty-check / compute shape. Tests cover known values, a single element, empty-input ValueError, and generators. python3 -m unittest discover -s tests: 10 tests, OK. Note only: stdev() lists and empty-checks, then variance() lists again and mean() lists once more. That second pass is over an already-materialized list, so generators stay safe, and the stdev empty check keeps its own error message. No change required.
